chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled in a case of two men who claimed a mule. One of them established two witnesses against his companion, and the other established five. So he ruled for the one with the five witnesses, five portions, and for the one with the two witnesses, two portions.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on a dispute where two parties presented different numbers of witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the principle of proportional justice in Shia jurisprudence, where the evidentiary weight of witnesses is not merely binary but quantitative. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) awarded five shares to the claimant with five witnesses and two shares to the one with two, demonstrating a flexible approach to testimony that values the quantity of credible witnesses. This ruling highlights the practical application of judicial discretion (ijtihad) in early Islamic courts to ensure equitable outcomes based on the strength of evidence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding two men who claimed a mule. So one of the two established two witnesses over his companion, and the other one, five. So he<sup>asws</sup> judged for the one with the five witnesses, five portions, and for the one with two witnesses, two portions’.
en.sarwar: 22. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from ibn Shu’ayb al-Muhamiliy al-Rifa‘iy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who hires a man to dig for him a well as deep as ten times the height of a man for ten dirham; but then he fails to do so because of weakness.
He (the Imam) said, ’Ten must be divided into fifty-five of which one is for the first length, two for the second and three for the third in the same way until the tenth.’”
